digitized specimens from a consented body donation program
constraints: Learners' exposure was restricted to 30 minutes of VR usage with planned breaks
navigational control was restricted to the purpose of the learning experience
target_learners: high school students aged 14-18 in informal pre-university science programs
target_learning_goals: introductory anatomy and neuroanatomy understanding
spatial understanding of 3D anatomical structures
examples: Learners in the Future Global Leaders program interacted with a library of 3D specimens including an interactive plastinated heart model with labeled structures, at least four times before completing surveys

citation: Santiago Elizabete Cristina de Lira; Dias Giulia Moreira; Timote Ana Clara de Sousa; Andrade Joanlise Marco de Leon; Ipolito Michelle Zampieri; Funez Mani Indiana. (2025). description: The article argues that scenario validity is a required quality step in simulation design, citing the International Nursing Association for Clinical Simulation and Learning standards, and states that "Validated scenarios are more effective in promoting undergraduate nursing students' knowledge when compared to non-validated scenarios". Its own two-stage CVI process, which caught weak debriefing items and produced revisions, is offered as a demonstration of this step. examples: The study's first validity stage identified debriefing items with I-CVI 0.38, which were removed or reformulated before the second stage reached adequate indices

article_title: Online assessment of medical students' communication competence in patient encounters: Validation of the VA-MeCo situational judgement test.
citation: Reiser S, Schacht L, Thomm E, Janssen L, Pittroff SID, Dörfler E, Schick K, Berberat PO, Gartmeier M, Bauer J. (2025). Online assessment of medical students' communication competence in patient encounters: Validation of the VA-MeCo situational judgement test. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0332957
title: VA-MeCo: a video-based online situational judgement test assessing medical communication competence with 11 scenarios and 117 rating items
description: The VA-MeCo is a video-based online situational judgement test for assessing medical communication competence in medical students, grounded in the Calgary-Cambridge Guide and the Munich Model of Professional Conversation Competence. It comprises "11 patient encounter scenarios ('tasks'), each featuring 3–5 embedded answer options, and three ratings per option", constituting 117 items rated on a 6-point effectiveness scale. Scores are derived by raw consensus scoring against an expert key; sub-scale scores on the three dimensions can be aggregated to a total MCC score. Its digital implementation allows administration to large groups online.
requirements: A scoring key based on expert judgements with strong rater agreement, developed in a previous expert study.
Participants must complete at least five of the eleven tasks for scores to be analysed, per the study's inclusion criterion.
constraints: The article notes further validation is needed, particularly predictive validity for communicative quality in actual patient encounters, which was not assessed in this study.
The test primarily addresses cognitive aspects of MCC; interaction with procedural and attitudinal dimensions requires further research.
target_learners: medical students across all phases of medical education
target_learning_goals: medical communication competence in patient encounters (advancing content, providing structure, building relationship)
examples: In the validation study, N = 395 medical students completed the VA-MeCo online (average 45 minutes) followed by validation questionnaires; sub-scale scores were correlated with cognitive, patient-interaction and personality measures.

article_title: From classroom to clinic: innovating radiotherapy treatment planning education through real-world end-to-end case study simulation with an anthropomorphic phantom.
citation: Genitsarios Ioannis, Jhagra Robin, Warn Clive, Xavier Jesrina Ann. (2025). From classroom to clinic: innovating radiotherapy treatment planning education through real-world end-to-end case study simulation with an anthropomorphic phantom. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06695-w
title: Variation Theory as a curriculum structuring principle for radiotherapy planning scenarios
description: The article employs Variation Theory to structure the curriculum with varied scenarios, emphasizing the need to experience different facets of a phenomenon so learners can pinpoint essential variables and deepen conceptual understanding. Presenting various tumour sizes, shapes, and locations, different immobilization techniques and scanning protocols compels students to adapt decision-making; the authors state this exposure "fostered their ability to identify important details and adjust to varying clinical circumstances". The article deems Variation Theory superior to Multiple Intelligences Theory for this domain owing to its empirical foundation.
requirements: Systematic variation across multiple scenarios such as different tumour characteristics, immobilization techniques, and scanning protocols
target_learning_goals: Discerning critical features of radiotherapy planning
Adaptable problem-solving across diverse clinical contexts

article_title: Assessing availability and trainees' perceptions of simulation and augmented reality in prosthodontics postgraduate education in Pakistan: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Khalid Taimur, Yaqoob Hassan, Syed Fakeha Azhar, Kazmi Syed Murtaza Raza. (2024). Assessing availability and trainees' perceptions of simulation and augmented reality in prosthodontics postgraduate education in Pakistan: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06542-4
title: Validated 8-item REDCap questionnaire on SBL and AR/VR availability and trainee perceptions
description: The study's instrument is an 8-item questionnaire disseminated via a REDCap weblink, asking trainees about availability of and access to SBL and AR/VR at their training centres and their perceptions of effectiveness and curriculum integration. It "underwent content validation by five subject specialists and one medical health professional", with each item receiving an Item-Level Content Validity Index score and modified kappa statistics of "≥ 0.82 for relevance and clarity". Respondents answered using 'Yes', 'No', or 'Don't Know' options.
requirements: Content validation by subject specialists with each item meeting I-CVI and modified kappa (k*) standards of ≥ 0.82 for relevance and clarity
constraints: Administered via email weblink to postgraduate prosthodontics trainees in Pakistan between May and October 2021; undergraduates, dental hygienists, supervisors, and other-specialty trainees were excluded
target_learning_goals: assessing availability and perceived effectiveness of simulation-based and AR/VR learning in postgraduate curricula
examples: Total population sampling yielded a sample of 200 participants, of whom 90 completed responses were analysed

article_title: Effect of problem-based learning on students' attitude towards learning physics: a cohort study.
citation: Kanyesigye ST, Uwamahoro J, Kemeza I. (2022). Effect of problem-based learning on students' attitude towards learning physics: a cohort study. F1000Research 11: 1240. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.125085.1
title: Views About Science Survey (VASS) P05.07 as an attitude measurement instrument
description: The Views About Science Survey is a standardized, non-multiple-choice attitude instrument developed by Halloun to distinguish "expert" and "folk" views of physics. The P05.07 version "contains 33 items that measure students learning outcome before and after covering a certain content", rated on a 5-point Contrasting Alternatives scale in 40 minutes. This study administered it to 419 Ugandan students, computing percent expert-like responses pre- and post-test.
requirements: Administered to students before and after instruction to compute the shift in percent favorable responses
Content validated by expert panel (CVR > 0.49) and piloted for internal consistency
constraints: A pilot Cronbach's alpha of 0.73 was reported; construct validity information was questioned by a reviewer
target_learners: secondary school physics students (13th grade, ages 16-21)
target_learning_goals: attitudes and beliefs about physics, expert-like scientific thinking
examples: Used to classify students into folk, transitional, and expert profiles across a Solomon four-group design in the 2021 Ugandan study

article_title: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery simulation and training: a comprehensive literature review.
citation: Grossi Sarah, Cattoni Maria, Rotolo Nicola, Imperatori Andrea. (2023). Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery simulation and training: a comprehensive literature review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-023-04482-z
title: Three-category taxonomy of VATS lobectomy simulators: wet, dry, and VR/AR-based systems
description: The review organizes VATS lobectomy simulators into three groups by the system used to recreate the human chest. As printed: "Simulators are classified into three groups according to the system used to recreate the human chest and its contents: wet simulators (animal tissues or live animals), dry simulators (synthetic lung models), and those requiring virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR)." The review then reviews validation evidence for each category separately.
requirements: Simulators must recreate the human chest and its contents in one of three ways: animal tissue, synthetic models, or VR/AR rendering
constraints: The review notes high heterogeneity in techniques and quantification of results across studies, so no category is established as most instructive
target_learning_goals: VATS lobectomy technical skills acquisition in a risk-free environment
